research_progress.source_confidence_semantics: Heuristic official-source research confidence only. Current GOV.UK, Natural England, Planning Inspectorate and Active Travel England pages checked on 25 July 2026. Public rights of way, definitive maps, CROW access land, commons/town-village-green registers, National Trails and coastal access remain at their published legal, procedural or route-management scope. They are not parcel-title rights, private easement opinions, development permissions, guaranteed access routes or Future Growth score accuracy.

source_facts.fact: GOV.UK distinguishes footpaths, bridleways, restricted byways and byways open to all traffic, with different permitted uses.
source_facts.gate: Route class must not be guessed from a generic path line or visual appearance.

source_facts.fact: Natural England guidance says the definitive map and statement is the legal record maintained by the highway authority.
source_facts.gate: A web map or OS depiction is not automatically the definitive legal record.

source_facts.fact: GOV.UK notes access may exist based on historic use or at least 20 years of public use even where standard mapped routes do not resolve the question.
source_facts.gate: No mapped route must not be converted into no public right of way.

source_facts.fact: Planning Inspectorate guidance states definitive map modification orders record legal rights; they do not themselves create or extinguish ways.
source_facts.gate: A pending or confirmed DMMO must be interpreted by its actual legal effect and evidence.

source_facts.fact: CROW access normally applies to mapped open country and registered common land, subject to excepted land and restrictions; public rights of way remain a separate legal right.
source_facts.gate: Open-access status must not be conflated with a footpath, bridleway, ownership or development right.

source_facts.fact: Natural England's June 2026 collection states there are 17 National Trails in England and Wales; route changes and diversions are managed through formal processes.
source_facts.gate: National Trail presence is not a title boundary or planning refusal and current diversions must be date-checked.

official_measurement_examples.name: Recorded PRoW route classes
official_measurement_examples.fact: Footpath, bridleway, restricted byway and byway open to all traffic have different permitted uses.

official_measurement_examples.name: Definitive map legal status
official_measurement_examples.fact: Highway authorities must maintain the definitive map and statement as the legal record of recorded public rights of way.

official_measurement_examples.name: Unrecorded rights caution
official_measurement_examples.fact: GOV.UK recognises that historic use or long public use can be relevant even where access is not resolved by standard mapped routes.

official_measurement_examples.name: DMMO legal effect
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Inspectorate guidance states DMMOs record existing legal rights and do not themselves create or extinguish ways.

official_measurement_examples.name: CROW access scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: CROW access normally applies to mapped open country and registered common land, subject to exceptions and restrictions.

official_measurement_examples.name: Common and green register structure
official_measurement_examples.fact: Commons registration authorities maintain separate registers for common land and town/village greens with mapped register units.

official_measurement_examples.name: National Trails current count

official_measurement_examples.name: Coastal access route management
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England says approved coastal routes can have restrictions, excepted land and formal variation processes.

core_rules: definitive map route is a legal record and must not be replaced by a convenience web map
online council or third-party map is not automatically the definitive map
absence from a map does not prove no unrecorded public right exists
historic user evidence may be relevant to unrecorded rights and must not be ignored
public right of way is distinct from a private easement
public right of way is distinct from permissive access
permissive access can be withdrawn and must not be reported as permanent right
footpath rights must not be expanded to cycling horse riding or motor vehicles
bridleway rights must remain distinct from restricted byway rights
restricted byway rights must remain distinct from byway open to all traffic
physical track width does not prove legal highway width
definitive statement may contain width or limitation evidence and must be checked where material
DMMO application is not a confirmed map modification
DMMO confirmation records rights and does not itself create a preferred new route
public path diversion and DMMO processes must remain distinct
temporary closure is not permanent extinguishment
planning permission does not automatically divert or extinguish a public right of way
development affecting a PRoW may require separate legal path procedures
PRoW protection and enhancement policy is not automatic refusal
route obstruction is not evidence that legal rights have ceased
CROW open access is distinct from public rights of way
CROW access land does not grant every recreational activity
excepted land can sit within mapped access areas and must be checked
CROW local restrictions can affect access temporarily or seasonally
registered common land is distinct from town or village green
common land ownership is distinct from rights of common
common-land register ownership entries must not be treated as conclusive title without appropriate checks
town or village green rights are not the same as general CROW right to roam
deregistration application is not deregistration approval
replacement-land requirements depend on the governing common-land process
common or green status is not planning permission
coastal margin access does not transfer ownership
coastal access can include excepted land without CROW access rights
coast path route can roll back or vary due to coastal change
National Trail line is not cadastral parcel geometry
National Trail route may change through formal diversion or order processes
trail GPX or visitor map is not a legal title plan
National Trail status does not mean every section allows cycling or horse riding
right to roam does not generally include cycling or horse riding absent another right or permission
local access restriction must be date-checked before reporting current availability
public access right does not establish vehicular development access
public pedestrian access does not prove adequate planning access for a development
access route existence does not establish ownership of the underlying land
local highway authority remains the primary source for definitive route evidence
NO_DATA must not be converted into no public access right
screening access evidence must remain separate from candidate promotion
no parcel access entitlement planning outcome or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
research-source confidence must not be reported as parcel legal-right accuracy
